patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Medusa and Shopware share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Comparison thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs. Choose Medusa only if your buying job matches “Headless JS commerce — MIT OSS free; Cloud Develop $29, Launch $99 highlighted, Scale $299” rather than Shopware's shape. Choose Shopware only if your buying job matches “Symfony open-source commerce — Community Edition free (Fair Usage ~€1M GMV); Rise from ~$6” rather than Medusa's shape. Workflow advantage: Medusa leans shared coverage; Shopware leans catalog-management, wholesale-b2b. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Medusa and Shopware share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Medusa is Headless JS commerce — MIT OSS free; Cloud Develop $29, Launch $99 highlighted, Scale $299, Enterprise custom. No GMV tax.; Shopware is Symfony open-source commerce — Community Edition free (Fair Usage ~€1M GMV); Rise from ~$660/mo; Evolve from €2400/mo; Beyond quote..
- Workflow coverage skew: Medusa-leaning — vs Shopware-leaning catalog-management, wholesale-b2b.
- Researched limits: Medusa — Headless means you still build or buy the storefront UX; Shopware — Community Edition Fair Usage pushes paid plans above ~€1M GMV.

Limitations — Medusa: Headless means you still build or buy the storefront UX; Not a WordPress-native plugin path (see WooCommerce); Shopware: Community Edition Fair Usage pushes paid plans above ~€1M GMV; Rise commercial floor is high versus WooCommerce core + hosting.

Poor-fit cases: Medusa is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Headless means you still build or buy the storefront UX · Shopware is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Community Edition Fair Usage pushes paid plans above ~€1M GMV · Avoid Medusa if you actually need Shopware's motion (Symfony open-source commerce — Community Edition free (Fair Usage ~€1M GMV); Ris)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
